subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Nasopharyngeal and salivary gland cancers: viral pathogenesis, staging and systemic therapy

steps.tx: **Nasopharyngeal carcinoma** is endemic across southern China and Southeast Asia, showing a pathogenetically distinct link with **Epstein-Barr virus** infection. The World Health Organization classifies the disease histologically into keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, non-keratinizing differentiated carcinoma, and non-keratinizing undifferentiated carcinoma type 3. The non-keratinizing undifferentiated type represents the most common variant in endemic regions and demonstrates exquisite radiosensitivity and chemosensitivity.
steps.say: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is endemic across southern China and Southeast Asia, showing a pathogenetically distinct link with Epstein-Barr virus infection. steps.tx: Quantification of circulating cell-free **EBV DNA** provides a reliable liquid biopsy **biomarker** in clinical management. Pretreatment plasma EBV DNA copy number correlates directly with gross anatomical tumour burden and occult micrometastases. Measuring clearance kinetics of plasma EBV DNA following definitive radiotherapy identifies patients harboring residual disease who require intensified adjuvant systemic chemotherapy.

steps.tx: Locoregionally advanced disease requires combined-modality systemic and radiation therapy. In phase 3 randomized trials, **Induction gemcitabine** plus **cisplatin** followed by concurrent **chemoradiotherapy** significantly improved recurrence-free survival and overall survival compared to concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone. Delivering upfront induction chemotherapy effectively eradicates distant micrometastatic disease and shrinks gross primary tumour volume.

steps.tx: Frontline treatment for metastatic disease incorporates cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside PD-1 checkpoint blockade. Adding **toripalimab** or **camrelizumab** to frontline **gemcitabine** and **cisplatin** chemotherapy significantly prolonged progression-free survival and overall survival in randomized phase 3 trials. This chemo-immunotherapy combination is now the established global standard of care for previously untreated metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

steps.tx: **Adenoid cystic carcinoma** is a distinctive salivary gland tumour characterized by the hallmark **MYB-NFIB** gene fusion. This fusion arises from the recurrent t(6;9) translocation and drives constitutive overexpression of the MYB oncoprotein. Clinically, the tumour exhibits an indolent natural history, prominent neurotropism with perineural invasion, and a relentless tendency for delayed pulmonary metastases occurring decades after initial surgical excision.

rows: Requires wide surgical margins and RT

steps.tx: **Mucoepidermoid carcinoma** is the most common malignant salivary neoplasm in both adults and children. Diagnostic molecular testing reveals the characteristic reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 11 and 19, specifically t(11;19), which creates the **CRTC1-MAML2** fusion transcript. Fusion-positive tumours typically present as low or intermediate histological grade lesions and correlate with a substantially more favourable long-term clinical prognosis.

steps.tx: **Salivary duct carcinoma** represents an aggressive high-grade malignancy that histologically and molecularly mirrors invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. Neoplastic cells demonstrate intense nuclear positivity for the **androgen receptor** in over 90% of cases and exhibit frequent HER2 gene amplification. Because of early lymph node metastases and systemic dissemination, comprehensive multidisciplinary staging and adjuvant therapy are essential.
steps.say: Salivary duct carcinoma represents an aggressive high-grade malignancy that histologically and molecularly mirrors invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. Neoplastic cells are positive for the androgen receptor in over 90% of cases and exhibit frequent HER2 gene amplification. Comprehensive multidisciplinary staging and adjuvant therapy are essential.

steps.tx: Biomarker-directed targeted systemic therapies provide substantial clinical benefit in advanced **salivary duct** carcinomas. Androgen receptor-positive tumours respond effectively to combined **anti-androgen therapy** utilizing **bicalutamide** or **enzalutamide** paired with GnRH agonists. Furthermore, tumours demonstrating HER2 overexpression achieve durable disease regressions with anti-HER2 regimens including **trastuzumab** combined with docetaxel or emtansine.
